August 09, 2026   |   Listen online   |   Read online

Good morning,

If you've been thinking about coming to Vancouver Tech Days Vol. 2 in October, don't wait. Vol. 1 sold out in five days and went over capacity — as of writing, we're already down to a limited number of tickets for round two.

Not sure if it's worth it? William wrote up five takeaways from Sarah Huggins' fireside chat at Vol. 1, where the Hiive co-founder made the case that Vancouver founders need to stop making self-defeating assumptions about building here.

The rest of the week's news is below.

—Emily

 
 

Events

 

Tech Days Vol. 2

Vancouver Tech Days is back for round two. Vol. 1 sold out in five days and went over capacity — proof that this city's builders want more than another networking mixer.

 
 

Office Hours with Vancouver Tech Journal

There’s no programming, no panel, no pitch stage. Just open time to connect, ask questions, share ideas, and meet other thoughtful people who care about building in Vancouver.

 
 

From The Journal

 

Tech Days recap: Five ways Hiive has thrived in Vancouver

Co-founder and COO Sarah Huggins on talent, culture, regulation and building a globally ambitious company from here.

 
 

BC Founders Day wants you to talk to strangers in leis — and it's working

Ahead of the August 20 event at South Flats, organizer Chris Neumann on why the world's most fragmented startup scene needed a founders-only meetup, and what "exceptional" looks like this year.

 
 

Top 25 Spotlight: IvoryOS Technologies

IvoryOS Technologies turns fragmented Python automation scripts into visual, drag-and-drop workspace with just a single line of code.

Vancouver Tech Journal • Guest Contributor

 
 
 

Funding, Deals, and More

  • Vancouver's Beedie Capital has acquired a 50% stake in Vistara Growth and will anchor its upcoming US$500 million structured opportunities fund, deepening a partnership that traces back to the two founders meeting as UBC MBA classmates in the early 1990s. Read more →

  • Vancouver-based Intellistake Technologies has signed a $17 million acquisition agreement for NanoAi Technologies, a Dallas-based nanotechnology company that has developed portable standoff detection devices with applications in defence, healthcare and critical infrastructure. Read more →

 
 

In Other News

  • Council of Canadian Innovators B.C. director Kiersten Enemark argues that B.C.'s planned patent box should extend beyond life sciences to cover clean tech, AI and advanced manufacturing — and that the province needs an Innovation Box, not just a patent box. Read more →

  • Vancouver city council has postponed a public hearing on a proposed AI data centre in Mount Pleasant until after the October municipal election, following nearly 600 public submissions and sustained community opposition to the project. Read more →
